title: Effective parameters and the precision-aware loss
goal: Section 4.2 models training in low precision as a smaller model. Each of the weights, the activations, and the KV cache contributes a factor $1 - e^{-P/\gamma}$ to $N_{\text{eff}}$ (Equation 4), and Section 4.1 puts $N_{\text{eff}}$ into the Chinchilla loss. The constants of Appendix K, Table 2 are defined in the starter. Write `eff_factor(p, gamma, offset=0.0)`, which returns $1 - e^{-p/\gamma + \text{offset}}$. Write `n_eff(n, p_w, p_a, p_kv, offsets=False)`, which returns $N$ times the product of the three factors, using `OFFSET` when `offsets=True` and zero otherwise. Write `loss_hat(n, d, p_w, p_a, p_kv, offsets=False)`, which returns $A N_{\text{eff}}^{-\alpha} + B D^{-\beta} + E$ with $\beta = \alpha$.
hints: `eff_factor` is one line: `1.0 - np.exp(-p / gamma + offset)`. Convert `p` with `np.asarray(p, dtype=float)` so that it accepts lists.
`n_eff` multiplies three factors, and each factor uses its own entry of `GAMMA` and `OFFSET`. The keys are `"w"`, `"a"`, and `"kv"`. Don't use one shared gamma.
When `offsets` is `False`, pass an offset of 0 to every factor. A quick check: with all three precisions at 4 bits and no offsets, $N_{\text{eff}} / N$ is about 0.639.
`loss_hat` is the Chinchilla form with `n_eff(...)` in place of `n`. The data term uses the same exponent `ALPHA`, because the paper ties $\alpha = \beta$ (Appendix K).
